text: The case state, the two case moves, the timer read and stop, the WO rule package and the placement of PLACED_WITH_AGENCY are consumed on their owners' published contracts, never as tables or views, and their operation names stay placeholders until the owners publish them.
why: Only rwb-case writes recovery_case and the timer, only rwb-decision governs the rule rows and the ledger, and the placement belongs to another owner. The legacy Data table names recovery_case, timer, partner, decision_log_entry and rule_row, none of which is this service's, while TSD S7 T5.2 names published interfaces only as module interfaces and publishes no operation name for a move, a timer stop, a package read or a placement read, so no name may be invented. The plan's C and I rows are empty, so these rows are class C in fact and not in the metadata.

impact: The app story builds on Day 1 against five contract fakes with a 2 s budget and a breaker, and a statement on a recovery_case, timer or partner row fails the boundary test

why: DP-04 is not in the pattern set the plan gives this key, yet the step evaluates R-WO-36, R-WO-47 and R-WO-48 of the WO route set of 51 rules over 27 states and the architecture places rule evaluation inside the owning service's activity. Keeping the plan's H row unchanged and recording the kit as a tracked dependency is the only choice that does not invent a metadata value.

text: The retention wait is a Temporal durable timer inside WriteOffWorkflow, so this step owns no Temporal Schedule, no Quartz row and no shared job table; the Workbench scheduler named by R-WO-36 and R-WO-47 is read as that timer, and JOB-16 stays the monthly scan of RWB-S7-E6013-APP.
why: Both rules name the Workbench scheduler, but DP-10 is absent from the pattern set of this key, the FSD declares the monthly scan as the module's only background event, and the only job the context pack gives the service is JOB-16. The architecture replaces Quartz with Temporal timers and Schedules, and a retention wait is a timer of one case, not a periodic job, so no job row, Schedule element or table may be invented.

text: The placement facts of PLACED_WITH_AGENCY, its ends_at and its recovered_amount, arrive with the case read or with a placement read that no source publishes; the legacy partner row of DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 is not read as a table here, and the operation name and the owner carry the placeholder.

Inventing a column or an operation would create a fact no document owns, so the read is declared as consumed with a placeholder.

text: The retention period of the timer and the retention classes of the documents are reference data and parameters read with their version; no source sets a period or a class list, so both carry the placeholder and neither is ever a constant or a schema default.
why: REQ-S7-008 says a case closes after its retention period without giving a length, NFR-028, NFR-030 and NFR-031 are open under DL26 and record the period as not set, and FSD S7 BR-S7-013 forbids a value a business person may change from being written in code. A length chosen by the builder would be an invented business value.

text: write_off.decision_log_id is written with the identifier the local decision-record library returns, and the P7 ledger entry identifier is not stored on the write-off row; the ledger entry itself is written by rwb-decision on the shared decision-record topic.
why: DF-FIN-012 is described as the decision_log_entry this record belongs to and decision_log_entry is P7's table, while DP-03 keeps a local record in the caller's transaction and P7 keeps the central ledger. Storing a foreign identifier the service cannot verify would be a value it cannot maintain, so the column carries the record this service writes and the ledger stays with its owner.

text: The cash recovered and the loss of the closing entry required by R-WO-47 are attributes of the local decision record; no column of write_off carries the loss, and recovered_after (DF-FIN-020) is not bound to either amount by any source.
why: R-WO-47 asks for a closing entry with cash recovered and loss, but TSD S7 T3.1 gives write_off one recovered amount field, recovered_after, with no field ID or description binding it to the closure, and no source gives the loss a column at all. Choosing a binding would be an invented accounting rule, so the two amounts are recorded on the entry and the binding stays open.
